scope: Construction review for two photographed training/development hearts. Does not alter images, material labels, split membership or historical benchmark counts.

cases.construction: The green sheet has closed interior regions marked for removal inside the bicycle wheels and frame. These are cut-out holes, in addition to the cuts joining the folded boundary and inner part of the paper.
cases.trainingUse: Still useful for visible-body and physical-paper identification; do not use as a regular-slit ground-truth template pair.
cases.pipelineInterpretation: The bicycle is present in the photographic mask and absent from the fitted weave. The published construction lies outside the current regular-slit model; this example alone is not evidence that longer regular fitting should recover the original paths.

cases.construction: The purple sheet has three closed interior regions marked for removal between the sloth limbs and the branch. The yellow sheet provides the complementary silhouette. The published pair uses cut-outs, beyond regular slits.
cases.trainingUse: Still useful for visible-body and physical-paper identification; do not use as a regular-slit ground-truth template pair.
cases.pipelineInterpretation: A low-error legal regular-slit approximation is not recovery of the published cut-out construction. Seam artifacts should be interpreted with this model limitation in mind.

limitations: The observations classify the published templates, not every possible alternative construction of the same visible design. No impossibility theorem for alternative slit arrangements is claimed.
The animal PDF also includes a rabbit design; its photograph differs from the reviewed Pinterest rabbit, so no exact template pairing is assigned to that instance.

Prior nineteen-photo studies retain their original denominator and per-case outcomes. Future regular-template comparisons should identify these cases separately, consistent with the user instruction to ignore irregular constructions.
